title: Audit cap table
summary: Audit the cap table before a raise: verify ownership, board consents, and investor rights are documented.

parts.title: Gather all investor documents
parts.guidance: Collect the executed documents supporting outstanding securities and investor rights, including subscriptions, SAFEs, amendments, side letters, grants, transfers and cancellations. Reconcile the collection to the cap table and financing receipts to locate missing evidence. Distinguish signed records from drafts and request absent documents from the responsible person so the audit covers every recorded position.

parts.title: Verify cap table accuracy
parts.guidance: Trace each holding and convertible balance to its supporting document and effective transaction. Recalculate class totals, reserve use and fully diluted views using the documented definitions, then compare with the equity platform and legal records. For each discrepancy, identify the affected position, evidence and proposed correction before changing the live data.

parts.title: Review board consents
parts.guidance: Match issuances, grants and other relevant equity actions to their corporate approvals. Have counsel assess authority, signatories, effective timing and terms under the governing documents. Distinguish a missing uploaded consent from an action that lacked authorization, and establish the appropriate remedy for each defect without backdating or fabricating the record.

parts.title: Attorney sign-off
parts.guidance: Give the attorney the reconciled cap table, supporting documents and unresolved findings. Obtain a conclusion stating the review’s scope, accepted corrections and legal work still required. Apply supported record corrections through the equity administrator and keep outstanding exceptions visible when sharing the audited table, so readers understand what the legal review actually covered.

metadata.supportReason: Verifying ownership and consents is judgment work with attorney sign-off; document gathering runs on the cap-table APIs.
